objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (17 November 2026), STATE-RULES-20261117-001's first direction, with its referee's lead and the owner's erasure question: does a cap on how many knots a distinction (or a pair of distinctions) may join stop the cheapest growth at two orders; which state differences separate matched starts with the same states and different knots, and do they persist; and what do the states remember after the knots are erased? Serves G1 and G16; tests A97 and A99.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; refereed R1, confirmed with fixes, one narrowing): the two natural caps (three knots per distinction, two per pair) stop the cheapest growth exactly at the 2 x 2 pattern (proved); looser caps pass two orders and no cap keeps two orders growing. How knots meet changes what grows and, for the five-starts (end hub vs middle hub), how many orders (exact); after erasure the six-starts' states keep a fading imprint (0.78 to 0.41 by n = 11, kept about 0.7), while the five-starts' difference fades with or without the knots. 4 of 9 predictions held.
stop_rule: One proof and one frozen computation with its read-out; A97 and A99 status; referee hand-off; report.
title: A cap on knots per distinction, and what matched starts remember
